title: Incomplete validation feedback
description: Multiple failures are present but the system directs attention to only one, leaving other required information unexplained.
trigger: Submit after clearing the name or email field.
observable: Submission is blocked, but the interface reports only that the password is invalid.

title: Password error lacks diagnosis
description: The error identifies failure without explaining the password requirement or how to correct it.
trigger: Press Continue with the supplied password.
observable: The message states only that the password is not valid.

title: Reset behaves unexpectedly
description: A broadly labelled Reset control does not produce the complete reset users would reasonably expect.
trigger: Press Reset after changing more than one field.
observable: Only the password field is cleared while the other form values remain.

title: Recovery request gives no immediate feedback
description: The user cannot determine whether the action succeeded, failed, or is still processing.
trigger: Press Send recovery link once.
observable: Nothing visible confirms that the request was received or processed.

title: Rate-limit error is unexplained
description: The user is told they cannot proceed without enough information to recover.
trigger: Press Send recovery link three times.
observable: A rate-limit message appears but gives no waiting period or recovery action.

title: Alternative account action has no result
description: An apparent escape route does not communicate or perform an outcome.
trigger: Press Use a different account.
observable: The control produces no visible change or navigation.

title: Unsaved changes are not indicated
description: The user cannot reliably distinguish saved state from edited state.
trigger: Edit either profile field without saving.
observable: The page provides no indication that the displayed values differ from the saved profile.

title: Profile navigation does not respond
description: Controls presented as navigation create an expectation of movement but provide no system response.
trigger: Press Overview, Contact, or Security.
observable: The apparent navigation controls do not change the view.

title: Reset is too close to save
description: The layout increases the chance and consequence of an accidental destructive action.
trigger: Edit the fields and press Reset changes.
observable: The destructive action sits beside Save and immediately clears the fields without confirmation.

title: Toggle appearance contradicts state
description: The control conflicts with an established interface convention, making state harder to interpret.
trigger: Compare the toggle appearance with its current state and change a setting.
observable: The visual convention for on/off is deliberately reversed from the familiar toggle pattern.

title: Secondary information dominates
description: Secondary copy interferes with rapid scanning of the primary controls.
trigger: Scan the notification options and identify their setting labels.
observable: The Partner offers explanation occupies disproportionate space compared with the setting itself.

title: Month navigation lacks directional cues
description: The user must infer navigation behaviour from neighbouring month names.
trigger: Inspect the controls either side of June 2026.
observable: The controls are labelled only May and Jul rather than communicating previous and next navigation.

title: Selected date has weak feedback
description: Important system state requires extra visual effort to recognise.
trigger: Select a date in the calendar.
observable: The selected state is only modestly distinguished within a dense grid of similar controls.

title: Changing date clears the selected time
description: Changing one choice unexpectedly destroys another choice and forces repeated work.
trigger: Choose a time, then choose another date.
observable: The selected time disappears without warning.

title: Selection controls behave inconsistently
description: Similar choices use different interaction rules without explaining why.
trigger: Try selecting several attendance options.
observable: Checkboxes and a radio control are mixed within one conceptual attendance group.

title: Capacity failure appears too late
description: The system permits an unavailable choice instead of preventing the error earlier.
trigger: Select Dinner and press Register.
observable: Only after registration is attempted does the interface reveal that Dinner is full.

title: Search submission is ambiguous
description: The user cannot confidently determine what the search action changed.
trigger: Change the query and press Search.
observable: Results briefly fade but no clear loading, completion, or changed-result state is shown.

title: Irrelevant result metadata dominates
description: Secondary information makes the primary identification task slower.
trigger: Scan the result list for the requested title.
observable: Record numbers, availability, collection and shelf metadata compete strongly with result names.

title: Sort selection does not reorder results
description: The control reports a new state that is not reflected in the content it claims to control.
trigger: Change Sort by to Newest or Alphabetical.
observable: The selected sort value changes while the result order remains unchanged.

title: Applied filter count hides filter identity
description: The user must remember prior selections to understand the current result state.
trigger: Apply one or more filters, then return to the results.
observable: The interface reports only how many filters are active, not which ones.

title: Filter panel closes after every choice
description: A repetitive interaction adds unnecessary steps to a common refinement task.
trigger: Open Filters and select an option.
observable: The panel closes after each filter change, requiring it to be reopened to make another adjustment.

title: Empty results do not explain the filter conflict
description: The empty state does not identify which constraints caused the dead end or how to recover.
trigger: Apply all three filters.
observable: The products disappear and the page states only No matching items.

title: Destructive actions compete with continuation
description: The interface increases the chance of choosing a consequential action accidentally.
trigger: Compare Remove/Clear cart with the Continue action.
observable: Destructive and progressive actions occupy the same immediate decision area with limited differentiation.

title: Cart total does not update with quantity
description: The system state shown to the user does not reflect the changed order state.
trigger: Change the Field Notebook quantity.
observable: The displayed order total remains $64.

title: Delivery cost is deferred from the decision point
description: Important cost information is visually subordinate and deferred until after the user begins committing.
trigger: Review the total and proceed toward checkout.
observable: Delivery is only described as being calculated later rather than incorporated into the current total.

title: Long checkout has no progress indication
description: The user has little sense of effort remaining in a constrained mobile viewport.
trigger: Scroll through Customer, Delivery and Payment.
observable: Several checkout sections must be completed without any overall progress or remaining-step indication.

title: Payment error does not identify the field
description: The user must diagnose the failure by guessing where corrective action is needed.
trigger: Press Pay now with the supplied payment value.
observable: A general payment error appears without identifying the invalid field.

title: Back action discards entered details
description: Moving backwards unexpectedly destroys entered information without warning.
trigger: Change the card number and press Back.
observable: The card value is cleared immediately.

title: File actions rely on ambiguous symbols
description: Recognition depends on interpreting unfamiliar or overloaded icon metaphors.
trigger: Inspect the icon-only file toolbar.
observable: Move, rename, upload and archive are represented only by symbols whose meanings are not consistently conventional.

title: Move operation gives no completion state
description: The system provides no visible status for a consequential file operation.
trigger: Select a file and press the move icon.
observable: Nothing indicates whether the file moved or where it went.

title: Rename can duplicate an existing filename
description: The system allows a potentially confusing naming conflict without prevention or warning.
trigger: Select Interview notes, choose Rename, leave Research summary as the new name and save.
observable: The rename succeeds even though another visible file already has the same name.

title: Upload requirements are incomplete
description: Necessary instructions are absent until a user potentially encounters a failure.
trigger: Inspect the upload interface before choosing a file.
observable: No accepted file type or size requirements are provided.

title: Progress stalls near completion
description: The indicator creates an unreliable impression of how much work remains.
trigger: Choose a file and observe the progress state.
observable: The progress display reaches 90% and remains there before completion appears.

title: Low-value information dominates the dashboard
description: Visual hierarchy does not reflect the information-seeking task.
trigger: Find the metric requested by the task.
observable: Large cards and a prominent support chart give similar or greater weight to unrelated information.

title: Key metrics require interpretation
description: Users must recall domain terminology rather than recognise plain-language meanings.
trigger: Interpret MRR, ATV, NRR and QA without external reference.
observable: Several metrics are presented only as unexplained abbreviations.

title: Sorting affordance is inconsistent
description: Comparable columns expose different interaction affordances without explanation.
trigger: Compare the Name, Status and Updated headers and try sorting.
observable: Name and Status are sortable buttons while Updated is plain text.

title: Row action feedback is absent
description: The user cannot tell whether the command was received or what it did.
trigger: Press View on any row.
observable: The apparent row action produces no visible result.

title: Bulk action gives no recovery information
description: A consequential bulk operation provides insufficient control or recovery.
trigger: Select one or more rows and press Apply to selected.
observable: The interface reports only Action completed, without naming the action, affected records, or offering undo.

title: Locate action overrides map exploration
description: A convenience action unexpectedly removes the user’s current navigation context.
trigger: Use + or - to alter the map, then press Locate.
observable: Locate recentres the map and overrides the explored position without preserving it.

title: Selected place is not reflected on the map
description: Two representations of the same selection communicate different states.
trigger: Press Select this place.
observable: The sheet changes to Selected location while the map marker itself remains visually unchanged.

title: Playback controls use ambiguous symbols
description: The symbols conflict with familiar play/pause conventions and the displayed media state.
trigger: Use the left playback control.
observable: The control initially shows || while the screen already says Playing, then changes to > when pressed.

title: Playback settings are not reflected in player status
description: The user must remember a setting rather than seeing its effect represented in the main player state.
trigger: Open settings and enable Subtitles or 1.5×.
observable: The checkbox changes but the player display gives no confirmation of the active playback setting.

title: Message send state is unclear
description: The user cannot determine the transmission state of the new message.
trigger: Press Send with the supplied message.
observable: The message appears in the conversation but has no sent, pending, delivered, or failed status.

title: Presence status is ambiguous
description: System language does not map cleanly to a recognisable real-world presence state.
trigger: Inspect the conversation header.
observable: The header states active 2m ago, combining a current-state term with elapsed-time wording.

title: Permission language is overly technical
description: Technical system language does not explain the permission in terms of the user’s goal.
trigger: Read the Nearby device discovery explanation.
observable: The description uses system proximity services and external device endpoints.

title: Denying one permission blocks unrelated work
description: Rejecting an optional-looking permission removes control over the broader task.
trigger: Press Deny for Nearby device discovery.
observable: The page states that the user cannot continue.

title: Help search results are poorly prioritised
description: Help content is available but ranked in a way that slows access to the likely solution.
trigger: Search for cannot submit assignment.
observable: The directly relevant Submission failed result appears after broader articles.

title: Troubleshooting action is buried
description: Important recovery information is harder to scan than surrounding explanatory material.
trigger: Read the Submission failed result.
observable: The actionable retry guidance appears after several prerequisite checks inside dense copy.

title: Cancellation language is ambiguous
description: Ambiguous wording increases uncertainty around a destructive decision.
trigger: Compare Keep booking with Cancel without keeping.
observable: The phrase without keeping does not clearly state what will be lost or retained.

title: Cancellation failure lacks recovery guidance
description: The error does not help the user diagnose or recover from the failure.
trigger: Press Cancel without keeping.
observable: The interface reports that cancellation could not be completed but gives no reason or next action.

title: Prerequisite is revealed after submission
description: Information that could prevent an unsuccessful action is disclosed only after the user commits to enrolment.
trigger: Select the Tuesday 14:00 class and press Enrol.
observable: The interface reports that the prerequisite is missing only after the enrolment attempt.

title: Prerequisite terminology requires interpretation
description: Abbreviations and institutional codes do not match the language a student needs to make a decision.
trigger: Read the eligibility information before enrolling.
observable: The course lists “PRQ: 120UOC + L2 progression” without explaining the terms.

title: Timetable conflict lacks recovery guidance
description: An error identifies a conflict but does not tell the user what is conflicting or how to resolve it.
trigger: Attempt enrolment while another class is scheduled at the same time.
observable: The message reports “CONFLICT 204” without naming the conflicting class or next step.

title: Displayed price changes after selection
description: The system presents a price that does not match the committed choice, undermining trust in system state.
trigger: Select the cheapest direct flight and continue to review.
observable: The fare changes from $189 to $227 after selection because a fee appears.

title: Comparison requires recall
description: Opening one result replaces its detail view with another, forcing the user to remember information while comparing options.
trigger: Select the 08:15 flight, inspect its details, then select the 09:40 flight.
observable: The details area replaces the first flight details with the second, so comparison requires remembering the first set of information.

title: Important fare condition is disclosed late
description: A restriction that affects the decision is revealed only after a flight is selected.
trigger: Select a basic fare and continue.
observable: A baggage restriction appears only after the fare is selected.

title: Default extra remains selected
description: A default option is applied even after the user chooses a configuration that suggests otherwise.
trigger: Choose the vegetarian burger, then review the selected extras.
observable: Cheese remains selected by default and is included in the order.

title: Customisation state disappears
description: The summary does not preserve information about meaningful user choices, making the final state difficult to verify.
trigger: Remove cheese, collapse customisation and inspect the order summary.
observable: The summary says only “Vegetarian Burger” and omits the no-cheese choice.

title: Removal control uses contradictory language
description: The interface describes a negative choice using an action word that implies the opposite operation.
trigger: Inspect the cheese option in the customisation controls.
observable: The control reads “ADD: No cheese”, making the intended action ambiguous.

title: Time period is ambiguous
description: The time field visually underemphasises whether the selected time is morning or evening.
trigger: Set the alarm to 07:30 and inspect the time display.
observable: The interface shows 07:30 without a clear AM/PM context or equivalent day cue.

title: Saved alarm lacks persistent confirmation
description: Closing the editor does not provide a clear indication that the new alarm now exists in the active list.
trigger: Save the 07:30 alarm and return to the alarm list.
observable: The editor closes but the resulting alarm is difficult to distinguish from the previous list state.

title: Save status contradicts document state
description: The interface communicates a saved state while changes remain unsaved.
trigger: Make a formatting change and inspect the save indicator.
observable: The header continues to read “Saved” immediately after editing.

title: Undo removes more than the last action
description: The system reverses multiple actions at once, reducing predictable control over editing.
trigger: Make two separate formatting changes, then press Undo once.
observable: Both formatting changes disappear after a single Undo action.

title: Formatting control loses active state
description: The control does not visually reflect a formatting state that is currently applied to the selection.
trigger: Select bold text and inspect the Bold control.
observable: The Bold control looks inactive even though the selected text is bold.

title: Permission terminology is unclear
description: Labels use organisational terminology that requires interpretation before a user can predict the resulting access.
trigger: Open the sharing permissions for Sam.
observable: Options such as Contributor, Participant and Collaborator are presented without plain-language definitions.

title: Default permission is overly permissive
description: The system chooses a higher level of access than is necessary for the requested task.
trigger: Open the sharing dialog for a new recipient.
observable: The default permission grants full edit access rather than the requested comment-only access.

title: Permission change applies immediately
description: A consequential access change occurs without a save, cancel or undo point.
trigger: Change Sam’s permission from Editor to Commenter.
observable: The permission changes immediately and the dialog offers no clear way to cancel the change.

title: Low-value information dominates
description: Visually prominent information competes with the weather details needed to answer the task.
trigger: Determine whether conditions are suitable for the 15:00 outdoor event.
observable: The large current-temperature display dominates while the relevant hourly forecast is secondary.

title: Weather abbreviations are unexplained
description: Domain-specific shorthand forces the user to infer meanings that matter to the task.
trigger: Inspect the 15:00 forecast details.
observable: The forecast exposes “PoP”, “DP” and “UV” without labels or explanations.

title: Departure and arrival modes are indistinguishable
description: Two different route time concepts use nearly identical visual treatments, increasing the chance of misreading.
trigger: Compare departure and arrival details for a suggested route.
observable: Departure and arrival are presented with the same hierarchy and styling.

title: Live delay does not update arrival estimate
description: System status shows a delay without updating the associated consequence, creating contradictory information.
trigger: Select a route showing a live service delay.
observable: The interface displays “+14 min delayed” while the arrival time still says 08:52.

title: Route comparison clears previous selection
description: Exploring an alternative route destroys the user’s previous selection without warning.
trigger: Select a route, then compare another route and return.
observable: The original selected destination/time is cleared when the route changes.

title: Recipient confirmation is insufficient
description: A consequential transaction is confirmed using identifying information that is too limited to prevent a mistaken recipient.
trigger: Review the transfer before submitting it.
observable: The confirmation shows only “A. Smith”, with no additional recipient identifier.

title: Transfer failure leaves transaction state unclear
description: The system reports failure without telling the user whether the transaction occurred or whether retrying is safe.
trigger: Submit the transfer with the supplied details.
observable: The message says “Something went wrong” without confirming whether funds moved.

title: Cancel action is ambiguous
description: The control does not clearly distinguish cancelling the transaction from leaving the transfer process.
trigger: Review the action controls before submitting.
observable: The control is labelled “Cancel transfer” even though it can exit both the transaction and screen.

title: Upgrade visually dominates downgrade
description: Unequal visual emphasis biases attention toward an action the user did not request.
trigger: Open subscription options and locate the Basic plan.
observable: Upgrade is presented as a large primary card while downgrade is a small secondary link.

title: Cancellation language obscures consequences
description: The interface uses promotional or indirect language instead of clearly naming the resulting action.
trigger: Review the wording around moving to Basic.
observable: The action is phrased as “Continue without Premium benefits” rather than “Downgrade”.

title: Downgrade requires unnecessary steps
description: A routine account change is stretched across multiple confirmations without adding useful information.
trigger: Attempt to change Premium to Basic.
observable: The user passes through repeated confirmation steps before the same choice can be submitted.

title: Selection state is weak
description: Selected media is difficult to distinguish from unselected media during multi-selection.
trigger: Select three photographs.
observable: The selection indicator is a subtle border that is easy to miss among similar thumbnails.

title: Move action is hidden behind an undisclosed gesture
description: An important action depends on a gesture the interface does not teach or signpost.
trigger: Try to move the selected photographs to the Fieldwork album.
observable: The Move action only appears after a long-press interaction with a selected image.

title: Drag target provides no affordance
description: The board gives little indication of where a dragged card can be released or what will happen.
trigger: Drag “Prepare critique” toward Done.
observable: No drop target or insertion cue appears while dragging the task.

title: Drop operation appears successful before reverting
description: The interface briefly communicates a successful state before silently reversing it, contradicting the user’s understanding of system status.
trigger: Click the “Prepare critique” task to place it on the Done board and watch the board for several seconds.
observable: The task briefly appears to move toward Done, then returns to its original position without explanation.

title: Priority uses inconsistent representations
description: The same concept is represented using incompatible labels in different parts of the interface.
trigger: Set the task priority to High and compare its representations.
observable: The board uses “!!!”, the editor uses “HIGH” and the filter uses “P1”.

title: Device state and action are ambiguous
description: A single label does not make clear whether it describes the current state or the action that will occur.
trigger: Inspect the bedroom light control.
observable: The control reads “OFF” without making clear whether the light is currently off or will be turned off.

title: Delayed response encourages repeated actions
description: Slow feedback invites repeated input, increasing the chance that the user unintentionally reverses the final state.
trigger: Tap the bedroom light control and observe its response.
observable: Nothing visibly changes for several seconds, so repeated taps can produce an unexpected final state.

title: Progress reflects navigation rather than completion
description: The progress indicator reports completion based on page movement rather than satisfying the actual task requirements.
trigger: Move through the questionnaire without answering every required activity.
observable: The interface reaches “100%” even though the embedded activity is incomplete.

title: Conditional requirement is undisclosed
description: A new mandatory question appears only after the user has already committed to an earlier answer.
trigger: Choose an answer that triggers a follow-up question.
observable: A mandatory explanation field appears without advance indication that more input will be required.

title: Previous answers are lost when navigating backward
description: The system discards user work during ordinary navigation and provides no recovery.
trigger: Answer several questions, navigate back and then forward again.
observable: Previously entered responses have been cleared.

title: Device icons do not clearly communicate state
description: The controls do not make clear whether an icon represents current state or the action that will occur on activation.
trigger: Inspect microphone and camera controls before joining.
observable: The crossed microphone icon could be interpreted as either muted or an instruction to mute.

title: Join state contradicts preview state
description: The system presents one device state in the preview and activates another state after commitment.
trigger: Set microphone off and camera on, then join.
observable: The preview shows the microphone muted, but joining activates it.

title: Progress is based on pages visited
description: The progress indicator communicates completion even though required activity has not been completed.
trigger: Use the navigation controls to move through the lesson without completing the quiz.
observable: The module reports 100% after pages are visited, despite an incomplete activity.

title: Next action becomes available too early
description: The system permits progression before required work is complete and only complains later.
trigger: Skip the required activity and try to continue.
observable: The Next button is available even though the lesson requirement is unmet.

title: Unavailable times disappear during comparison
description: The system removes alternatives after a selection, making it difficult to compare options without remembering them.
trigger: Compare several available reservation times before selecting 19:00.
observable: Once 19:00 is selected, other options disappear from view.

title: Modification confirmation resembles a new reservation
description: The completion message does not distinguish an updated booking from creation of a second booking.
trigger: Change the reservation and confirm the modification.
observable: The confirmation simply says “Reservation confirmed” without saying the existing booking was changed.

title: Return selection is spatially ambiguous
description: The relationship between the selection control and product row is unclear, increasing the risk of acting on the wrong item.
trigger: Select the black notebook for return.
observable: The checkbox sits between product rows rather than clearly belonging to one item.

title: Return stages are unexplained
description: The system names process stages without clarifying what each state means or what the user should expect.
trigger: Review the return status after submitting the request.
observable: The sequence “Requested → Processing → Pending → Accepted” is shown without explanations.

title: Back navigation loses the return reason
description: Ordinary navigation discards information the user has already supplied and provides no recovery.
trigger: Enter a return reason, press Back, then use the return form again.
observable: The return reason has disappeared when the form is revisited.

title: Settings provide no preview
description: The user cannot immediately see the practical effect of a visual setting before committing to it.
trigger: Increase text size and inspect the interface before saving.
observable: The settings change only takes visible effect after leaving the page or saving.

title: Negative toggle wording creates ambiguity
description: Double-negative or inverted wording increases the cognitive effort required to predict the setting state.
trigger: Review the reduced-motion setting.
observable: The control reads “Disable reduced motion: OFF”, requiring the user to reason through the negation.

title: Immediate action visually dominates scheduling
description: Visual hierarchy promotes an irreversible or disruptive action over the less disruptive alternative.
trigger: Choose between installing now and scheduling tonight.
observable: “INSTALL NOW” is visually dominant while “Schedule” is secondary text.

title: Update consequences are disclosed after selection
description: A meaningful consequence is revealed only after the user selects the action that causes it.
trigger: Select Install Now and review the next step.
observable: Only after selection does the interface reveal that the computer will be unavailable for approximately 45 minutes.

title: Scheduled state omits the scheduled time
description: The system reports that an action has been scheduled without communicating the specific state needed to verify it.
trigger: Schedule the update for tonight and review the confirmation.
observable: The message says “Update scheduled” without stating when it will run.

title: Paid plan is preselected
description: The interface uses a normal-looking selection state to steer the user toward a paid plan they did not explicitly request.
trigger: Begin the free trial and inspect the plan selection before continuing.
observable: The annual paid plan is already selected while the free-trial option is visually secondary.

title: Trial-to-paid transition is visually subordinate
description: A consequential billing condition is present but deliberately given less visual weight than the attractive free-trial call to action.
trigger: Review the trial summary before accepting it.
observable: The trial invitation dominates the page while the later charge is presented as low-emphasis supporting text.

title: Cancellation information is deferred
description: Information about how the user can stop the paid continuation is not presented where the commitment is made.
trigger: Inspect the terms presented at the point of starting the trial.
observable: The commitment explains the trial and payment but provides no immediate cancellation route or guidance.

title: Optional baggage is preselected
description: An optional paid service begins in an active state, increasing the chance that it will be accepted without deliberate choice.
trigger: Review the add-ons before continuing with the flight booking.
observable: Checked baggage is already selected even though the task asks for no additional services.

title: Insurance appears in the final summary
description: An optional service is allowed to enter the purchase summary without a distinct affirmative selection step.
trigger: Continue through the add-ons and review the booking summary.
observable: Insurance appears in the summary even though it was not deliberately selected as a separate action.

title: Declining extras has weaker visual hierarchy
description: The interface presents both choices, but visual emphasis strongly favours acceptance.
trigger: Compare the controls for accepting or declining optional services.
observable: The affirmative option is filled and prominent while the decline route is quieter and less noticeable.

title: Accept all visually dominates
description: The consent interface gives the broadest data-sharing option the strongest visual priority.
trigger: Review the available consent choices without selecting one.
observable: Accept all is the dominant button while more restrictive options are visually subordinate.

title: Reject option is hidden among secondary links
description: The restrictive choice is technically available but is presented as a low-emphasis text action rather than a peer choice.
trigger: Look for a way to continue without enabling optional data use.
observable: The reject or configure route is visually embedded among low-priority links.

title: Several purposes are bundled together
description: One broad action changes multiple consent purposes at once, reducing the user's ability to choose precisely.
trigger: Open the consent choices and attempt to allow necessary data use without enabling all optional purposes.
observable: The recommended action enables multiple purposes together instead of offering equivalent granular choices.

title: Countdown timer does not represent a real deadline
description: The interface creates urgency by displaying a disappearing deadline that does not actually govern the offer.
trigger: Watch the sale countdown expire before completing the purchase.
observable: The timer reaches zero and the sale remains available.

title: Scarcity claim lacks a verifiable quantity
description: The interface suggests limited availability without providing information that allows the claim to be evaluated.
trigger: Review the product availability messaging before purchasing.
observable: The page says the jacket is selling fast but does not provide a concrete stock figure.

title: Cancellation path is much longer than sign-up
description: The user must pass through multiple retention-oriented steps to perform a straightforward cancellation.
trigger: Follow the available controls from subscription management toward cancellation.
observable: The cancellation route passes through several unnecessary screens and options.

title: Cancellation reason is mandatory
description: The system adds an unnecessary requirement between the user and an otherwise available account action.
trigger: Attempt to continue cancellation without choosing a reason.
observable: The interface requires a reason before allowing the user to proceed.

title: Final cancellation action is visually subordinate
description: The interface preserves the desired action but makes the service-provider-preferred alternative substantially more prominent.
trigger: Review the final cancellation choice.
observable: Keep my membership is the prominent action while Continue cancellation is visually understated.

title: Notification prompt returns after dismissal
description: The interface repeatedly interrupts the user to encourage an action they already declined.
trigger: Dismiss the notification prompt, then continue creating the task until the prompt returns.
observable: The same prompt reappears after the user has already chosen Not now.

title: Dismissal is temporary rather than meaningful
description: The interface provides a temporary escape but no clear way to permanently decline the request.
trigger: Look for a lasting way to stop notification prompts.
observable: The only refusal option postpones the prompt rather than recording a meaningful preference.

title: Fee appears only at the final step
description: A mandatory cost is withheld until the user has invested effort in the purchase process.
trigger: Proceed from the product page through the checkout stages and compare the advertised price with the final total.
observable: The final total is higher because a mandatory fee appears only at the last step.

title: Fee description obscures its meaning
description: The label uses vague terminology that makes it harder to understand why the additional charge exists.
trigger: Read the line item added to the checkout total.
observable: A vague label such as Service facilitation adjustment is used instead of a plain-language fee description.

title: Final total has weaker hierarchy than product price
description: The price users initially notice is given stronger emphasis than the amount they will actually be charged.
trigger: Compare the product price with the final amount shown before payment.
observable: The original product price remains more visually prominent than the final payable total.

title: Refusal uses emotionally loaded language
description: The interface frames refusal as a socially undesirable choice rather than presenting it neutrally.
trigger: Review the wording of the newsletter refusal option.
observable: The refusal says something like No thanks, I prefer to miss important stories.

title: Acceptance is framed as responsible behaviour
description: The affirmative choice is associated with being informed and responsible while declining is framed negatively.
trigger: Compare the language used for accepting and declining the newsletter.
observable: Accepting is framed as Keep me informed while declining carries a negative social implication.

title: Activity message implies popularity
description: The interface presents synthetic social activity as evidence that the product is currently desirable.
trigger: Inspect the product activity messages before deciding whether to purchase.
observable: A message claims that a specific number of people are viewing the product despite the activity being deliberately synthetic.

title: Scarcity and social proof reinforce each other
description: Multiple urgency signals are combined to encourage a purchase without giving the user reliable evidence for the claims.
trigger: Review the stock and activity messages together.
observable: The interface combines Only 2 left with a message about other people having the product in their cart.

title: Recommended download is the paid version
description: The interface uses familiar download conventions to steer users toward a different product from the one they requested.
trigger: Find the free version of the software and inspect the primary download options.
observable: The most prominent Download button leads to a paid version while the free version is available elsewhere.

title: Advertisement resembles the product interface
description: A promoted product is styled so closely to the genuine download options that its commercial status is easy to overlook.
trigger: Compare the visual treatment of the sponsored option with the genuine download choices.
observable: The promoted option uses the same card structure, controls and hierarchy as the real product options.

title: Free option receives weaker explanation
description: The requested free option is technically present but receives less useful information and lower visual emphasis than the paid option.
trigger: Compare the information provided for the free and paid versions.
observable: The paid version has the clearest description and strongest visual emphasis while the free version requires closer inspection.
